Dear Dr. Bennett,

Thank you for evaluating this 52-year-old male accountant for clinical consultation.

He recently underwent workup demonstrating marked aneurysmal dilatation of his aortic root. Echocardiography confirmed prominent root ectasia with myxomatous prolapse of the mitral leaflets and moderate mitral valve insufficiency. The aortic valve coapted well with no backward regurgitant flow, and there was no evidence of a dilated cardiac myopathy. CT angiography revealed no dissection involving the descending thoracic or abdominal aorta, and neither the abdominal aorta nor iliac vessels showed aneurysmal dilation. Carotid and vertebral arteries followed linear courses without tortuosity, and head CT showed no subdural blood accumulation. Chest imaging excluded free pleural air. Electrocardiography showed regular sinus rhythm without rhythm disturbances or partial right bundle branch block.

On examination, he is of average height with well-preserved muscle volume, lacking tallness or diminished muscular bulk. Early history was negative for neonatal floppiness. He exhibits mild osteoarthritic joint changes in his hands, but fingers lack flexion contractures. His spine has no scoliotic lateral curvature or vertebral slippage, and there is no history of developmental hip dysplasia, clubfoot deformity, or bunions. His skin lacks abnormal velvety softness, dermal translucence, or lower limb varicosities.

Craniofacially, his skull is not dolichocephalic, lacking frontal bossing, an elevated forehead, or an elongated face. There is no midfacial retrusive deformity, receding lower jaw, or low-set ears. His sclerae are white without a blue hue, ocular spacing is normal, palpebral fissures lack downward slant, and he has no drooping eyelids, proptotic globes, or ocular deviation. The palate is intact without clefting, the philtrum is neither smoothed out nor shortened, and dentition shows no crowding or deep overbite.

I appreciate your expert assessment and guidance.

Sincerely,
Dr. Vance
